marker.description: A thread tied around a nerve winding around the fibular neck.

main_question: Identify the structure indicated by the thread.
main_explanation: The thread is tied around the common fibular nerve (also known as the common peroneal nerve) as it winds around the neck of the fibula. This nerve is a terminal branch of the sciatic nerve.

supporting_question.question: Which of the following is a common clinical manifestation of injury to the indicated structure?
options: Loss of sensation over the medial leg
supporting_question.explanation: Injury to the common fibular nerve (common peroneal nerve) typically results in foot drop, characterized by weakness or paralysis of the muscles that dorsiflex the foot (tibialis anterior, extensor digitorum longus, extensor hallucis longus) and evert the foot (fibularis longus and brevis). This leads to the inability to lift the front part of the foot, causing it to drag during walking.

true_false.statement: The common fibular nerve is a terminal branch of the femoral nerve.
true_false.explanation: The common fibular nerve is a terminal branch of the sciatic nerve, which itself is a branch of the sacral plexus. The femoral nerve is a branch of the lumbar plexus.
